angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 493,947 km at 67.70 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.7719 +/- 0.0188 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 67.70 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.71 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Barragán et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-233 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.522.3458B/abstract): 493,947 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.79 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Barragán et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-233 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.522.3458B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4796 +/- 66 K from Barragán et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-233 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.522.3458B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barragán et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-233 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.522.3458B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-233.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.633, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
